gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, with a SIM you buy yourself, Reolink names only AT&T and T-Mobile prepaid data-only plans for the Go PT Ultra (Verizon is reachable only through the bundled multi-carrier SIM), and Reolink warns that phone-only plans may not work. eufy says the S330 accepts any data-only nano SIM and that its bundled EIOTCLUB SIM picks the strongest of AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon. So at a site where only Verizon has signal, the plan works only if the shopper keeps the bundled SIM (Reolink or eufy) or puts a data-only plan in the eufy.
standout_why: Compared against homesecurityradar.com/guides/security-cameras-without-wifi, smarthomeexplorer.com/guides/best-cellular-lte-security-cameras-no-wifi-2026, our own dealectric page and the cited Reolink pages. Home Security Radar already gives the bundled-SIM carrier lists (AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon auto-select for both eufy and Reolink) and the identical US LTE band list B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71, so bands are not new. Smart Home Explorer has one Slickdeals owner saying the eufy 'only works with the EIOT sim', which our eufy source contradicts. No rival page separates the bundled SIM from your own SIM. None says Reolink leaves Verizon off its own-SIM list, and none says phone plans may fail when data-only or IoT plans work. The cited Reolink product page does carry the carrier list, but none of ChatGPT's seven answers repeated it; they all said only 'verify AT&T, Verizon, or T-Mobile support'. That gives partial overlap and a modest edge.
decides: This confirms the eufy S330 as the safer pick when the shopper's only signal is Verizon or they want to bring their own SIM: eufy accepts any data-only nano SIM and its bundled SIM includes Verizon. The Reolink Go PT Ultra is fine on AT&T or T-Mobile prepaid data-only plans. On Verizon it is safe only with Reolink's bundled SIM and Reolink's own data. On every model the shopper should buy a data-only or IoT plan, not add the camera to a phone plan. All three Reolink, eufy and Arenti 4G models are cellular-first and record on motion events, not 24/7.

findings.value: "The camera does not support WiFi connection"; "It does not supports 5G or 2G SIM card"; 3G supported but "not recommended"; US LTE FDD B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71
findings.source_title: [Official] Reolink Go PT Ultra - 4G Solar Camera with 4K Pan & Tilt
findings.note: Cellular is the only link, so a dead SIM or plan means no remote access at all. Recording is 'motion-triggered' to microSD up to 128 GB. No 24/7 mode is listed. The page showed no price today.
